title: POPF-Prevent - Intestinal vacuum therapy for the prevention of postoperative pancreatic fistula A feasibility trial In partial pancreatoduodenectomy with reconstruction by pancreatojejunostomy (Lomgmire-Traverso), intraoperative transnasal insertion of a negative pressure drain wrapped with Suprasorb foil into the biliodigestive loop at the level of the pancreatojejunostomy. Continuous suction treatment for 5 (-7) days (critical phase of anastomosis healing) with active drainage of pancreatic juice and bile and utilization of the positive effects of Vacuseal therapy on anastomosis healing. Transnasal removal of the tube by manual traction.
summary: This is a technical feasibility study on the prophylaxis of postoperative pancreatic fistulas in the context of pancreatic head resection. The plan is to insert an intraoperative drain under suction into the biliodigestive loop at the level of the pancreatic anastomosis. This is intended to actively drain aggressive digestive secretions, while at the same time bringing the wound edges closer together, improving wall tension and reducing the tendency to edema and so improving tissue perfusion.

interventions.name: 20 consecutive patients with pancreatic head resection (regardless of indication) and reconstruction by pancreatojejunostomy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pathological (resectable) findings in the pancreatic head with indication for pancreatic head resection (benign and malignant tumors, chronic pancreatitis) and intraoperative decision to create an end-to-side pancreato-jejunostomy.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of patient consent. 
Minors. 
Adults unable to give consent.
Emergency intervention.
Pregnant women.
